newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weaker, but off day's low.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weaker, but off day's low.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed slightly weaker at 26.381 to the dollar despite late-session dollar selling which lifted it off the day's low, traders said.
The peso dropped to 26.385 in early trade, down from Wednesday's close of 26.378, after the Central Bank cut its overnight rate by one percentage point in the morning.
The peso's fall was stopped after the Central Bank intervened and sold dollars at 26.385.
"The peso recovered to 26.383 and 26.384 by lunch time," one trader said.
However, the Central Bank adjusted its dollar selling rate to 26.383 in the afternoon, prompting banks to change tack thinking the Central Bank was nudging for a stronger peso.
The peso went up to 26.380 before settling at 26.381 at close.
Traders expected the peso rate to appreciate next week as the Central Bank reverts its intervention rate to 26.375 and 26.379 levels.
The 26.385 rate was set in anticipation of a dollar-buying spree for the usual weekend arbitrage play.
